text: VinUniversity is a private, not-for-profit university established by Vingroup – the largest private conglomerate in Vietnam. We offer a variety of undergraduate and graduate programs in a wide range of disciplines, all taught in English by world- class faculty. Our students come from all over the world, creating a diverse and vibrant learning environment.

Our international students are not just part of the VinUniversity family, they are ambassadors of their cultures and essential contributors to our global dialogue. At VinUniversity, we celebrate this diversity daily, ensuring that every voice is heard and every perspective valued. Together, we’re not just building a university, we’re creating a global community of leaders, thinkers, and innovators.

This handbook is designed to provide you with the information you need to know to make the most of your time at VinUniversity. We encourage you to read it carefully and refer to it often. WELCOME TO VINUNIVERSITY 1

4 SEASONS IN HANOI Spring (February - April) This is widely considered the most pleasant season in Hanoi. Expect comfortable temperatures ranging from 23°C to 28°C with low humidity and occasional light drizzles. It's a perfect time for sightseeing and exploring the city's outdoor activities. Winter (December - January) Temperatures can drop as low as 6°C with dryness. We suggest you wear warm clothes and apply moisturizer, such as lotion and lip balm.

Autumn (September - November) Autumn brings a gentle shift, with temperatures ranging from 22°C to 28°C. Humidity dips, making it perfect for outdoor adventures. This season boasts stunning fall foliage and offers a great balance for sightseeing and cultural experiences. Summer (May - August) The hottest and most humid months in Hanoi. Temperatures soar between 30°C to 38°C with frequent afternoon showers.
You should wear light, breathable clothing and be prepared for rain showers by carrying umbrella or water-resistant jacket. 8

Welcome to Hanoi, Vietnam! You have just arrived and now you’re on your way to get your student visa and your baggage. Your venture towards VinUniversity starts right after you step out the airport. Unsure of what to do when you arrive? Here is a step-by-step guide on what to do after you land at Noi Bai airport. IMMIGRATION PROCEDURES & AIRPORT PICKUP SERVICE 1.

Prior Arrangements: Admission Confirmation: Ensure that you have received an official Letter of Acceptance from VinUniversity admission office. In case you haven’t received any, contact admission@vinuni.edu.vn. Visa Approval Letter: Before heading to your local airport, make sure to collaborate with the Admissions Office to obtain a visa approval letter from the Vietnamese Immigration Department. This letter is essential for visa processing upon arrival.

Passport & Photos: Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your stay; carry two passport-sized photos (typically 4x6 cm with a white background). 2. Upon Arrival at Noi Bai Airport: Follow Arrival Signage: As you disembark, follow the “Arrivals” signs to the immigration area. Proceed to the Visa on Arrival Counter: Follow signs directing you to the 'Visa on Arrival' or 'Landing Visa' counter, located before the immigration checkpoints.

Submit Required Documents: Visa Approval Letter: Present the original or a printed copy. Passport: Ensure it's valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay. Completed Entry and Exit Form (NA5): Forms are available at the counter; alternatively, the Admissions Office may provide this in advance. Passport-Size Photographs: Typically, two 4x6 cm photos with a white background are required. 10

Locate Your Carousel: Check the display screens to identify the carousel assigned to your flight. Keep your baggage claim tags handy for verification and for you to easily locate your luggages from the carousel. Final Checks: After clearing customs, make sure you have all your belongings, your customs declaration receipt (if applicable), and any other documents before exiting the terminal. Collect Your Luggage: Once you see your baggage, claim it and proceed to the final check.

If any luggage is missing or delayed, immediately visit the Airlines staff at their Lost and Found; or Noi Bai Airport Security Center at hotline 0243.5842627 or Lost and Found Department - Noi Bai International Terminal at hotline 0983774546, Email: taisanboquen@gmail.com for assistance. Follow Signage: After clearing immigration, follow the clear signs directing you to the baggage claim area, typically located on the first floor.

Proceed to Ground Transportation: Follow the signs to the exit, where you’ll find various ground transportation options such as taxis, GrabCars, or shuttle buses to reach your destination; VinUniversity! 3.

BANKING AND CURRENCY EXCHANGE There are several banks all across Vietnam that can help you with your financial state when you arrive. They offer services like currency exchange, receiving money, and using their designated apps for your transaction all through your life here in Hanoi, Vietnam. Opening a bank account is quite easy and can be completed in a few steps. Most of these banks have the same requirements so it’s not hard to open your own bank account for your transactions.

Language barrier isn’t a problem since banks around Hanoi usually have a designated teller who can help you with your transactions. Listed below are some of the ways you can get banking services and currency exchange for your financial needs.

Steps in opening a bank account Visit the local bank you chose to open your account with Most of the banks around Hanoi and Oceanpark have staffs that can speak english so you won’t have to worry about the possible language barrier Gather the required documents Make sure to gather all the required documents above to ensure a smooth process when opening your account Complete the application forms Fill out the designated application forms that the bank teller will give you.

In case you don't understand certain information, don’t be shy to ask the bank teller. Asking a vietnamese friend to accompany you is also a great idea to ensure you can easily fill out these forms. Receive your account detail and account activation After completing these steps, you can wait until the bank can process your account activation. These typically last for a few minutes to 14 days depending on the bank you choose.

To ensure a smooth bank transaction for your account, it is recommended to download the designated app from your bank account. ATM cards can usually be acquired only after living in Vietnam for a few months. 15

Currency exchange Exchanging currency in Hanoi is straightforward. Noi Bai Airport has several currency exchange booths, and their English-speaking staff make the process easy for foreigners. Alternatively, you can exchange currency at local banks (such as those listed above) after opening an account. While you might need some identification documents, the process of converting your currency to Vietnam Dong (VND) is generally quite simple. Different banks across Vietnam 16

DORMITORY REGISTRATION GUIDE VinUniversity provides on-campus accommodation for all students as part of its co-living and co-learning model. To register for dormitory housing, follow the steps below: Receive Accommodation Information All students will receive an official notification via their VinUni email regarding dormitory registration. This notification will include a dormitory registration form, outlining available accommod-ation types, housing policies, and submission deadlines.

Complete the Dormitory Registration Form Students must fill out the dormitory registration form within the specified deadline. In this form, students can indicate their accommodation preferences, including: Preferred apartment type (8-bed, 4- bed, or 2-bed apartment). Roommate preferences (if applicable). Any specific requirements related to accommodation.

Dormitory Assignment & Confirmation The Student Housing Office will review applications and assign accommodations based on availability and diversity considerations (college, nationality, and hometown). First-year students will receive a confirmation email with details about their dormitory placement, move-in date, and check-in procedures. Move-In & Orientation Upon arrival, students must check in at the Dormitory Management Office to receive their room key and dormitory regulations.
A dormitory orientation session will be conducted to help students settle in and understand dormitory policies. 19

ACADEMIC & REGISTRAR-RELATED INFORMATION VinUniversity provides students with a seamless and well-structured course registration process to ensure an optimal learning experience. Timeline: Course registration opens before each semester begins. Students must adhere to the published deadlines to secure their preferred courses. How to Register Students must register for courses through the VinUniversity Student Information System (SIS) Portal.

Detailed course offerings and descriptions will be available on the student portal. Consult your academic advisor before finalizing your course selections if needed. Course Load & Requirements Undergraduate students are typically required to enroll in a minimum of 12 credits per semester. The maximum credit limit per semester is 20 credits, unless special approval is obtained. Students must ensure they meet the prerequisites for each course before registering.

Course Retake Policies Students who fail a course may retake it in subsequent semesters. Retaking a course may affect GPA calculations and tuition fees. Overload Credit Approval: Students wishing to enroll in more than the standard credit load per semester must seek approval from the Registrar’s Office. Add/Drop & Withdrawal Deadlines: Add/Drop period typically lasts for the first two weeks of the semester. Withdrawal deadlines vary by course but are usually set in the middle of the semester.
Withdrawn courses may have tuition adjustments based on the university’s refund policy. 29 Course Registration Process

VinUniversity follows a semester-based system with clear term start and end dates. Credit Requirements Each program has a specified number of credits required for graduation. Students should review their degree plans with academic advisors to ensure timely completion. Graduation Review Process Students must submit a graduation application and ensure all academic requirements are met. Required documents include: Completed degree audit. Clearance forms from university departments.

Processing time for graduation approval may take up to several weeks. International students may need to transfer credits or take academic leave. Policies include: Academic Calendar & Graduation Process Credit Transfer Students must submit an official transcript from a recognized institution. The approval process involves: Course syllabus review. Determination of equivalency by faculty.

Procedural Guidelines for Credit Transfer Requests: Academic Leave of Absence Approval is required from both the academic department and the Registrar’s Office. Leave duration may be limited to a maximum of two semesters. Procedure for Requesting a Leave of Absence: 30

It offers an immersive experience where students can explore global traditions without leaving campus. 40

COMMUNICATION APPS & STAYING CONNECTED In Vietnam, the go-to messaging app is Zalo, a Vietnamese instant messaging platform developed by VNG Corporation, widely used for both personal and professional communication. Messenger is also a popular choice for staying in touch with locals. For social interactions, Instagram and Facebook are great platforms to connect with peers and stay updated on campus life.

However, while WhatsApp is rarely used among locals, it remains a bridge among international students, especially those still getting familiar with Vietnam’s preferred communication apps. For formal collaboration on group assignments and projects, Microsoft Teams is the go-to platform. Its versatile features, including video calls, file sharing, and real-time document collaboration, make it an essential tool for efficient teamwork and seamless communication among students. 41

HISTORICAL & CULTURAL LANDMARKS Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Distance from VinUni: 45 minutes A significant historical landmark, this is the final resting place of Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam’s revered revolutionary leader. Visitors can pay their respects and witness the solemn Changing of the Guards ceremony, a tradition that reflects Vietnam’s deep respect for its past.

Temple of Literature Distance from VinUni: 45 minutes With over 1,000 years of history, this ancient Confucian temple once served as Vietnam’s first university. The beautiful courtyards, stone steles, and traditional architecture make it a must-visit for history lovers and students alike. Hoa Lo Prison (Maison Centrale) Distance from VinUni: 40 minutes Originally built by the French to imprison Vietnamese revolutionaries, this historical site later held American POWs during the Vietnam War.

Known as the "Hanoi Hilton", it’s a sobering yet essential place to learn about Vietnam’s past struggles and resilience. Dating back over a thousand years, water puppetry brings Vietnamese myths, legends, and daily village life to life on stage.

The Quintessence of Tonkin Show Distance from VinUni: 60 minutes A breathtaking live performance that blends traditional folk elements with modern creativity, this must-see cultural show offers a mesmerizing experience of the Red River Delta’s rich heritage. Hanoi Old Quarter Distance from VinUniversity: 45 minutes Explore the 36 ancient streets that have preserved their history and architecture since the 19th century.

From unique shops and vibrant markets to centuries-old houses, the Old Quarter is a must-visit for shopping, sightseeing, and trying local street food. Hoan Kiem Lake Distance from VinUniversity: 45 minutes A favorite spot for locals and tourists alike, this lake is a peaceful escape in the heart of Hanoi. Whether you're walking, exercising, or just enjoying the view, it’s the perfect place to experience Hanoi’s charm. SCENIC & RELAXING SPOTS 43

Duong Lam Ancient Village Distance from VinUniversity: 60 minutes This 1,200-year-old village is home to houses dating back up to 400 years!

Its laterite and mud-brick structures offer a fascinating glimpse into Vietnam’s traditional rural life.
